newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL, Richter pushes BUX up.
newsitem.headline: MOL, Richter pushes BUX up.

text.p: Hungarian oil company MOL and pharmaceuticals firm Richter shares powered ahead on Wednesday, driving the Budapest Stock Exchange up after two losing sessions, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 5,965.43 points, up 101.00.
"MOL's price announcement was the main driving force today," one trader said.
MOL shares soared more than eight percent to close at 3,490 forints after a pricing in its six-times oversubscribed global offering took place late on Tuesday at $16.25 and 2,970 forints.

"The issue price had been a factor of uncertainty and by dispelling that uncertainty many investors, including foreigners, decided to buy on fears that lower numbers of shares would be allocated to them than what they were hoping," the trader said.
But another trader said earlier that expectations of strong first quarter earnings by MOL were also behind the rise.

Analysts expected MOL to remain the main market moving factor in the next few days, at least until after the release of its Q1 earnings report, depending on whether it meets expectations of a strong first quarter.

"I expect MOL to continue to rise, although possibly accompanied by some pauses," said Peter Postenyi, analyst at Raiffeisen Securities. "However, I don't think MOL's domestic subscription will substantially influence the market."
MOL's domestic public offer will start on May 12.
Richter was another driving force on Wednesday as it surged to new record of 14,525 forints in Budapest and $79 in London, benefiting from MOL's rally and its good Q1 earnings released last week.

"I think the oversubscription in MOL's global placement reminded investors that Hungarian equities are good," one trader said earlier. "Now, those companies which had really good results, like Richter, are rising along with MOL."
Traders said external factors, such as the Dow's movements or the dollar, added little to the market's overall pattern.
Chemicals company Borsodchem dipped 10 forints to 6,590 after the release of its Q1 consolidated HAS earnings report, as it was overshadowed by MOL and Richter.
Borsodchem released Q1 results earlier today with its after-tax profit rising 3.9 percent to 1.758 billion forints.
The market's other chemical company TVK which fell in the past few days recovered in what traders said was a late reaction to its Q1 earnings it had released on Monday.
